title: Reading a velocity-time graph
canonical_question: How do you read acceleration and distance off a velocity-time graph?
summary: On a velocity-time graph the vertical axis is velocity and the horizontal axis is time.
The area between the line and the time axis gives the distance travelled.

reuse.rationale: Authored fixture node for the E05 registry.

sections.heading: Slope is acceleration
sections.body_md: On a velocity-time graph the vertical axis is velocity and the horizontal axis is time. The steepness of the line, its slope, tells you the acceleration. A rising line means speeding up, a falling line means slowing down.

sections.heading: Area is distance
sections.body_md: The area between the line and the time axis gives the distance travelled. For straight-line segments this is just triangles and rectangles you can add up. So one graph yields both acceleration and distance.

key_points: Slope of the line is acceleration.
Area under the line is distance.
Rising means speeding up, falling means slowing.
core.bridge_to_parent: It is a graph-reading how-to, not a concept contrast.
